paragraphs: Tom and Ben walked out of the classroom after the meeting. "That was a long meeting," said Ben. "But now we all have a part in the class play." "I am the king's helper," said Tom. "And Hugo is the king," said Ben. "Hugo?" asked Tom. "But he is so shy!"

"I know, but our teacher decided," said Ben. "Hugo is quiet, but he is not the type of boy who gives up." "What do you mean?" asked Tom. "He writes every word of the play in his notebook," said Ben. "He reads it again and again, and he never forgets a line." "That is careful work," said Tom. "And he has some experience," said Ben. "Last year, he was a tree in the school show."

"A tree?" said Tom, and he laughed. "Yes, but he stood very still, and nobody laughed at him," said Ben. "What kind of character is the king?" asked Tom. "He is a kind king who loses his crown," said Ben. "He talks to everybody, and he has a big voice." "A big voice?" said Tom. "Hugo has a very quiet voice." "Maybe he will surprise us," said Ben.

"What about you, Ben?" asked Tom. "I am the cook, and I sing a funny song," said Ben. "I feel a little nervous," said Ben. "You?" said Tom. "You are the loudest boy in the school." "Yes, but I do not like to sing alone," said Ben. "I will stand next to you on the stage," said Tom. "Thank you," said Ben, and he smiled.

On Friday, the class had the first practice in the school hall. Hugo put on a gold paper crown, and he stood in the middle of the stage. The other children sat on the floor and waited. Hugo stood very still for a moment. "Hello, my people!" he said clearly. His voice was big and strong, and the hall went quiet. Everybody clapped, and Ben shouted, "Hooray for the king!" Tom looked at his friend and smiled. A shy boy can have a very big voice.
